title: Introduce adaptive baseline calibration CI gate for cohort-aware regression checks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add adaptive baseline calibration for eval CI gates to reduce false positives from cohort drift; configurable via eval-ci config. Backwards compatible by default (opt-in).
description:
Background and motivation: Our existing regression gate compares current cohort metrics against a fixed baseline percentile. This has produced a spike of noisy CI failures for long-tailed cohorts and for workloads with shifting traffic patterns. This PR introduces an adaptive baseline calibration stage in the CI hook that (1) estimates per-cohort baselines using an exponentially weighted rolling window, (2) applies conservative uncertainty bounds for small-sample cohorts, and (3) exposes a tunable "alpha" parameter and minimum-sample thresholds so teams can opt into stricter or looser gating.

What this PR does (summary): Adds a new CI hook `adaptive_baseline_gate` which runs as a pre-eval step in the existing eval CI workflow. The hook calculates cohort-aware baselines for configured metrics (e.g., accuracy, BLEU, F1, calibrated log-likelihood) and produces adjusted thresholds that replace the static baseline used by the regression guard. The PR includes: code for baseline estimation, unit and integration tests, updated CI workflow YAML, docs for config entries, and a migration helper to backfill baseline state for active cohorts.

Design notes: - Rolling estimator: EWMA on daily cohort aggregates with configurable decay (default half-life 14 days). This stabilizes baselines while remaining responsive to real shifts. - Uncertainty handling: For cohorts with fewer than `min_samples` (default 50), we widen the gate by a factor computed from the empirical variance + a tunable safety margin. - Backfill: We added a lightweight backfill job that loads the last 90 days to seed the estimator for active cohorts. Backfill runs once as part of the canary rollout; it is idempotent. - Config: `eval-ci.yml` gains a new section `adaptive_baseline` with fields `enabled`, `alpha_decay`, `min_samples`, `safety_margin`, and `cohort_whitelist`.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for estimator edge-cases (zero variance, single-sample cohorts). - Integration test that runs the CI hook on a synthetic dataset with three cohort behaviors (stable, seasonal, sudden-shift) and asserts gate firing rates match expected tolerances. - Ran the new hook against the last 30 days of historic eval runs from staging; reduced false-positive gate triggers by ~62% on a sample of 120 cohorts.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag disabled by default. 2) Opt-in small set of services (canary) and run backfill. 3) Monitor gate false-positive rate and eval success rate for two weeks. 4) Flip default to enabled with extended safety_margin if metrics are stable.

Notes for reviewers: - The main behavioral surface is `eval/hooks/adaptive_baseline.py`. It reuses existing eval-db queries and respects cohort tagging. - I added a simple CLI utility `tools/eval_baseline_backfill.py` for kicking off the backfill; this is separate from CI path. - I intentionally kept the default conservative so the hook is low-risk when enabled.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Documentation snippet in docs/ci_hooks.md
- [x] Backfill tool

Related: ENG-4821 (reduce CI noise from cohort drift), SUP-3312 (on-call escalations during holiday traffic).

review_comments: Priya Raman: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a short-circuit for cohorts with deterministic labels where variance is effectively zero? (2) Add telemetry tags so we can filter baseline backfills in dashboards.
Maya Chen (author): Added deterministic short-circuit and emitted `baseline.source` and `baseline.backfill` tags to the existing eval metrics. Updated tests to cover zero-variance case.

Luca Moretti: Please ensure we don't double-count backfill in EWMA when backfill and live data overlap — looks like current backfill seeds but doesn't mark the seed window. Add a marker or use epoch offsets.
Maya Chen (author): Backfill now writes `seed_epoch` with last_date to state row; estimator ignores entries older than seed_epoch on subsequent backfills. Added unit test for idempotency.
Samir Patel: Integration test looks heavy — can we reduce runtime by mocking DB queries? Also confirm the safety_margin default is conservative enough for low-traffic cohorts.
Maya Chen (author): Integration test retains one full path but uses smaller synthetic shards to keep runtime ~30s. Kept safety_margin=1.5 default; documented rationale in docs/ci_hooks.md.
